chains.title: G-allele TCF7L2 binding increases MYC enhancer output
chains.element: The rs6983267-containing 8q24 regulatory element acts as an enhancer for MYC.
chains.cell_type: Colorectal cancer cells, including HCT 116 cells with active Wnt signaling.

links.claim: TCF7L2 (also called TCF4) is the leading TF because prior work at this locus reports allele-sensitive TCF7L2 binding; the reference G allele is favored over T. No case-specific QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here.
The variant lies in an 8q24 regulatory element whose enhancer activity is greater with the G allele.
The element increases MYC expression, the best-established candidate target of the rs6983267 enhancer.
In colorectal cells such as HCT 116, Wnt/β-catenin signaling can support TCF7L2-dependent enhancer activity.
Higher MYC expression could promote colorectal tumor development, making the G allele the risk-increasing allele under this model.

predictions: At the same genomic background, changing G to T will reduce enhancer output and MYC transcription.
The variant-containing element will show preferential TCF7L2 occupancy on the G-bearing allele.
falsified_if: Isogenic G-to-T editing leaves MYC transcription and enhancer output unchanged in an adequately powered colorectal-cell assay.
Allele-resolved occupancy or binding assays show no G preference for TCF7L2.

chains.title: G-allele TCF7L2 binding increases CCAT2 expression
chains.element: The rs6983267-containing regulatory region within the CCAT2 locus acts in cis on CCAT2 transcription.
chains.cell_type: Colorectal cancer cells, including HCT 116 cells.

links.claim: TCF7L2 is the leading TF based on prior locus-specific allele-sensitive binding reports; the reference G allele is favored over T. No case-specific QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here.
The variant-containing region acts as a cis-regulatory element for the overlapping CCAT2 long noncoding RNA locus.
Greater activity of the G-bearing element increases CCAT2 expression.
In colorectal cancer cells, increased CCAT2 could influence oncogenic Wnt-related programs.
If the CCAT2 change is consequential, the G allele could increase colorectal cancer risk through CCAT2 rather than primarily through MYC enhancer output.

predictions: Isogenic G-to-T editing will reduce CCAT2 transcription; this effect should be more direct or larger than any primary change in MYC.
Perturbing the element will alter CCAT2 expression in cis.
falsified_if: Isogenic G-to-T editing has no reproducible effect on CCAT2 transcription.
Element perturbation changes MYC but not CCAT2 expression.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs6983267
predictions: Editing G to T will not produce a reproducible TF-dependent change in MYC or CCAT2 expression.
Any disease association may reflect a linked causal variant or another mechanism rather than an effect of this base.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-dependent effect is demonstrated by isogenic editing and is attributable to TF binding at this element.

matrix.test: Isogenic G-to-T editing in HCT 116 followed by nascent-RNA or RT-qPCR measurement of both MYC and CCAT2

outcomes.outcome: MYC decreases; CCAT2 need not show a primary change.
CCAT2 decreases; MYC need not show a primary change.
Neither transcript shows a reproducible editing-dependent change.

matrix.test: Allele-resolved TCF7L2 CUT&RUN or ChIP at rs6983267 in a heterozygous colorectal cell line

outcomes.outcome: Greater TCF7L2 occupancy on the G-bearing allele.
Greater TCF7L2 occupancy on the G-bearing allele.
No reproducible allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy attributable to this variant.

matrix.test: Perturb the variant-containing region and measure enhancer-promoter contacts to MYC and CCAT2

outcomes.outcome: The region preferentially engages the MYC regulatory domain.
The region acts in cis at the CCAT2 locus, without a dominant MYC contact.
No functional contact change attributable to the element.

next_experiment: The cheapest direct discriminator of the two leading chains is isogenic G-to-T editing in HCT 116 followed by measurement of both MYC and CCAT2 RNA. A selective MYC decrease favors H1; a selective CCAT2 decrease favors H2. Include unedited and mock-edited controls.
